title: Madison Common Council president rules out reelection, mayoral run - Channel 3000
text: MADISON, Wis. — Common Council President Sabrina Madison said Sunday that she will not seek reelection as the District 17 alder or run for mayor. Madison, who has represented District 17 since October 2022, made the announcement amid speculation that she would enter the mayoral race. Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway recently told News 3 Now in an exclusive television interview that she would not seek reelection. Madison said she has accepted a job outside Wisconsin that begins in August. "It's an opportunity that represents something different for me, and I'm excited about exploring it," she said. Alder Madison has pushed for police body cameras in the city following the fatal shooting of Corey Ruiz in July. Late last month, the common council president joined 13 other alders in voting to fire interim independent police monitor Aeiramique Glass. Madison also said she will begin studying journalism in January and looks forward to spending more time with her family. ​COPYRIGHT 2026 BY CHANNEL 3000. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. title: Wisconsin Governor Race: Tiffany and Crowley Rally in Madison - The Capital Times
text: In the final days of the race for Wisconsin Governor, David Crowley and Tom Tiffany both made bus tour campaign stops within 24 hours of each other in Madison. Both candidates have been zigzagging the state in custom-wrapped campaign vehicles - Crowley's a tour bus and Tiffany's a camper. Each event drew modest crowds of approximately 60 people and included a Halloween costume or two. On Halloween, Crowely and running mate Sarah Godlewski arrived to the Northside Action Team office on Sherman Avenue around 3 p.m. In addition to Crowley and Godlewski, supporters heard remarks from Sen. Tammy Baldwin, former chair of the Democratic Party of Wisconsin Ben Wikler, Attorney General Josh Kaul, candidate for State Treasurer Yee Leng Xiong, candidate for Secretary of State JoCasta Zamarripa, Dane County Executive Melissa Agard and Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford, candidate for Wisconsin’s 76th Assembly District. At 1:15 p.m. the following day, Tiffany's RV pulled into the parking lot of the Republican Party of Dane County office on Madison's West side. The gubernatorial hopeful arrived to a group of protestors from Indivisible, including two people wearing inflatable beaver costumes. Speakers for Tiffany's camp included former Governor Tommy Thompson, Sen. Ron Johnson and candidate for Attorney General Eric Toney. Both candidates shook hands with and smiled for selfies with supporters before embarking on the next leg of their individual journeys to election day. Wisconsin chapters from the Indivisible movement protest as Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany arrives in his campaign camper. Sarah Godlewski and David Crowley, candidates for Lt. Gov. and Gov. of WI wave to supports as they arrive at a WisDems canvass launch in Madison. In Godlewski's remarks, she referred to Crowley as her "future work bestie." Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany leans against his touring motorhome as he listens to remarks by former Governor of Wisconsin, Tommy Thompson before taking the stage himself. Melissa Agard, Dane County Executive and Sarah Godlewski, candidate for WI Lt. Gov. have a long embrace as Godlewski and Gubernatorial candidate David Crowley arrive at event. Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany stands by as Sen. Ron Johnson gives voters reasons to vote Republican in the fast-approaching mid-term election. Tracy Lewis holds a “Dogs for Democracy” placard as she crouches beside her dog, Gabby and listens to the campaign speeches. 18-month-old Alana applauds along with the audience as she attends a Tom Tiffany rally with her parents, just 2 days before the mid-term elections. “Moby” the dog wears a progress pride harness while attending the WisDems Crowley/Godlewski get out the vote bus tour stop in Madison. At a Republican Party of Dane County voter rally, Tommy Thompson, Former Governor of Wisconsin addresses the crowd, commenting that it might be serendipitous that his initials, T.T. are the same as Tom Tiffany’s. U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin applauds for Sarah Godlewski, candidate for Lt. Governor during the WisDems tour stop in Madison. Wisconsin chapters from the Indivisible movement counter-protest Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany's campaign stop in Madison. JoCasta Zamarripa, candidate for WI Secretary of State, shows gratitude to U.S. Rep. Mark Pocan while handing him the microphone at the WisDems event. Eric Toney, candidate for Wisconsin Attorney General elaborates on his experience with a 2023 open-heart surgery as he addresses supporters at the event. Sarah Godlewski, David Crowley, JoCasta Zamarripa and Lee Leng Xiong, all democratic candidates running for election, applaud for Rep. Mark Pocan during a WisDems canvass launch in Madison. Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany emphasizes Milwaukee Brewers team manager Pat Murphy's coaching style while discussing the importance of accountability. David Crowley, who is currently serving as the Milwaukee County Executive, addresses the rising costs of groceries, gas, utilities and childcare during the campaign stop in Madison. Gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany moves around the crowd, shaking hands with supporters and fellow Republican politicians. Gubernatorial candidate David Crowley hands out candy to children who stopped by the Halloween canvass launch with their parents. 6-year-old, Gracie smiles for the camera after her father placed a “Make America Great Again" (MAGA) hat on her head for the photo at the Tom Tiffany campaign rally. Yee Leng Xiong, candidate for Wisconsin state Treasurer, talks about his parents' challenging journey as refugees during his campaign speech. Several supporters wear “Team Tiffany” hats as they attend the campaign event in Madison. Attorney General Josh Kaul talks about his track record and plans if he is re-elected at the WisDems rally. Tom Tiffany stands in the middle of a group portrait in front off the campaign’s touring camper before departing the event.
